_doc: Taint semantics for external/library functions consumed by the bn taint engine. Keys are symbol names (leading underscores / common decorations are stripped when matching). Grammar for from/to: 'arg:N' = value of the Nth (0-based) argument, '*arg:N' = the buffer the Nth argument points to (its pointee variable), 'ret' = return value, '*ret' = the buffer the returned pointer points at. As a 'to' token (in 'propagates' or 'sources') '*ret' taints BOTH the returned value and that buffer, the buffer keyed by the CALL SITE (the same ('heap', call_addr) identity a recognized allocator's call gets, so a pointer re-derived from this call -- a copy, an indexed cursor, a PHI entry -- re-resolves to it); '*ret' is not accepted as a 'from' token. 'sources' seed taint; 'propagates' move taint from->to when 'from' is tainted; 'sink.tainted_args' lists argument indices whose taint is reportable, with a 'class' bug-class hint. Only '_comment'-prefixed keys are documentation and are ignored; any other '_'-prefixed key is a real model (e.g. '__isoc99_scanf', '__builtin_bswap32') that both the engine and the catalog resolve. A user override at the path from paths.taint_models_path() is merged over these.

models._comment_return_bound: return_bound.max_from_arg N: the return value (bytes received) is provably <= the constant in arg N (the count). Lets forward taint downgrade `m = read(fd,buf,MAX); memcpy(dst,buf,m)` from overflow to bounded_len with source_bound=MAX (#159).
models._comment_recv_overflow: read/recv/recvfrom/pread(fd, buf, len): the length (arg2) written into buf (arg1) can overflow an undersized destination. Modeled as an OPT-IN bounded-write sink gated behind `--sink-class recv_overflow` -- NOT always-on: a firmware measurement (#499) found ~100% false positives, because the dominant idiom `n = read(fd, buf+progress, cap-progress)` derives its length from the call's own return-value source, so the sink arms itself on a provably-bounded length. Enable it only when deliberately hunting recv-into-fixed-buffer overflows; the finding still reports class `overflow_len`.

sink.detail: attacker-controlled length written into buf via read()
attacker-controlled length written into buf via recv()
attacker-controlled length written into buf via recvfrom()

models._comment_recvmsg: recvmsg/recvmmsg scatter the received bytes into the iovec buffers at arg1->msg_iov[i].iov_base (recvmmsg: arg1[0].msg_hdr.msg_iov...), NOT a direct buffer arg. '*iovec:N' resolves the msghdr at arg N through the statically-set msg_iov and iov_base fields to the filled buffer(s) (#306); when the iovec setup can't be resolved the seeder falls back to an honest nudge.
models._comment_fgetc: Byte-at-a-time file/stream sources (CWE-121-style hand-rolled token/parse loops). Without these, fgetc/getc/getchar are unmodeled calls and a hand-rolled `while ((c = fgetc(f)) != EOF) buf[i++] = c;` loop shows only coarse_memory_store leaves with no modeled source in the catalog. Each returns a single int (the byte read or EOF) -- seed the return value, not a buffer arg.
models._comment_scanf_family: scanf-family DESTINATION seeding (#809). Unlike the printf family, whose varargs are DATA sources, the scanf varargs are POINTERS TO DESTINATIONS that the call fills: scanf(fmt, &a, &b, ...) fills args 1..N, fscanf(f, fmt, &a, ...) fills args 2..N, and sscanf(str, fmt, &a, ...) fills args 2..N from str's buffer (arg0), which is why sscanf propagates rather than sources. WHICH argument is a destination depends on the format string's conversion specifiers, and the model grammar has no token for 'every trailing pointer arg' -- so a fixed run of destination arguments is declared instead, and that run is what a `--source call:scanf` preset / `--source arg:sscanf:0` run actually seeds. FOUR destinations are unrolled (the arity real parse code overwhelmingly uses, e.g. `sscanf(buf, fmt, &a, &b, &s)`); a call whose format consumes MORE destinations than the unrolled run is NOT seeded past that point, and the grammar cannot attach a per-call caveat -- so the family's models declare 'arity_capped' and the ENGINE discloses the residual: a call whose param count exceeds the unrolled run makes it emit a 'scanf_arity_residual' weak-seed assumption, which withholds 'safe_to_report_all_clear'. A zero-sink run against a deeper format is a model limit, not a clean parse. (vsscanf's destinations sit behind a va_list and are deliberately unmodeled -- see _comment_vsscanf.) This is the honest-partial shape the family already uses (readv seeds only its return). The C99 spellings glibc actually exports are kept in lock-step with their base key so the fix is not bypassed by a compiler emitting __isoc99_*.
models._comment_vsscanf: vsscanf(str, fmt, ap): the destinations are reached through the va_list (arg2), not through the call's own arguments, and the engine has no resolver for a va_list's saved-argument area -- so its destinations are deliberately NOT claimed. It is modelled with the same honest-partial shape as readv: what IS recoverable is seeded (a tainted input buffer at arg0 propagates into the assigned-field count returned), and the copy into the caller's destinations stays unmodelled rather than falsely covered. `--source call:vsscanf` therefore fails loudly ('no taint-model sources to seed') instead of producing a confident empty result.
models._comment_line_readers: Line/blob readers that fill a caller buffer and return a length. getline/getdelim SET *lineptr (arg0 is char**), so `*arg:0` seeds the returned line buffer; without these `getline(&line,&n,f); system(line)` has NO taint origin -> a confident false all-clear. pread mirrors read (fills arg1, count=arg2). readv scatters into a RAW iovec array (arg1) that the msghdr-based `*iovec` resolver cannot key, so only its return length is seeded -- an honest partial model, not a silent miss. mmap is deliberately NOT modeled: a blanket `*ret` source false-positives on anonymous mappings, and unmodeled its return is already conservatively tainted by the default policy.

sink.detail: attacker-controlled length written into buf via pread()

models._comment_kernel_user_copy: Linux user<->kernel copy helpers (#809). On a statically-linked .ko a `bl copy_from_user` renders as an EXTERN_PTR stub that taint_il.const_target already name-resolves (taint_il.py), so without these models the call sites in the kernel's own copy-in path resolve to nothing. The DIRECTION is per function and deliberately ASYMMETRIC -- it follows where the untrusted bytes come from, not the argument order: the user->kernel pair (copy_from_user, get_user) SOURCES the caller's kernel-side buffer, because the bytes written into it are attacker-controlled user memory no matter how the user pointer itself was computed (the same reasoning as the read/recv/fread family); the kernel->user pair (copy_to_user, put_user) only PROPAGATES an already-tracked kernel buffer into the user destination and seeds nothing of its own. Swapping the two roles would either invent taint on a kernel->user copy or drop it on a user->kernel one. get_user(x, p) passes its destination lvalue BY ADDRESS (arg0) with the user source at arg1, so its source is `*arg:0`; put_user(x, p) passes the value by argument (arg0) and writes through the user pointer (arg1), so its propagation is `arg:0 -> *arg:1`. The kernel's exported spellings are exactly these names (glibc-style LFS64 `...64` suffixes do not exist here), so only the pre-existing lookup_model leading-underscore/@plt strip applies -- `__copy_from_user`/`_copy_from_user`/`__get_user`/`__put_user` resolve to these keys and no unrelated user symbol can borrow them (#603).
models._comment_parser_search: Parser-family string searches (#809). Each one RETURNS a pointer INTO the buffer it was handed (or NULL), so the taint edge is buffer -> the RETURN, never buffer -> a destination: modelling e.g. strchr as `*arg:0 -> *arg:1` would taint a caller-side output buffer that the function does not write, and would hide the real fact that the token/pointer a parser keeps is the tainted one. `ret` is the right token for a returned pointer here -- _apply_to_token collapses `ret` and `*ret` onto the call's written SSA vars -- and a downstream read through the returned pointer is then satisfied by the ordinary scalar/pointee checks. strstr's return aliases the HAYSTACK (arg0), not the needle, so only arg0 is declared. strtok_r(str, delim, saveptr) also publishes the next token pointer into the caller's saveptr (`*arg:0 -> *arg:2`) and, on the continuation call (str == NULL), tokenizes from that saved pointer (`*arg:2 -> ret`); strsep(&sp, delim) writes its advanced pointer back into the same slot it read the string from and returns a token from that buffer, so `*arg:0 -> ret` covers it (the write-back carries the same taint, no extra edge). DISCLOSED LIMIT: strtok keeps its cursor in libc-INTERNAL static state, which no model can key, so a bare `strtok(NULL, d)` continuation call resolves with no model-derived taint -- such a call is unmodeled-input, not proof of a clean parse.
models._comment_sort_search: qsort/bsearch (#809), the two libc routines whose interesting argument is a COMPARATOR CALLBACK that libc -- not the caller -- invokes. qsort(base, nmemb, size, cmp) permutes the caller's array IN PLACE and calls cmp (arg3) back with pointers into that array; bsearch(key, base, nmemb, size, cmp) RETURNS a pointer into base (arg1) or NULL and is therefore modelled like the str* search family above (base -> return; the key only steers the search, the returned bytes come from base). MODELLED: qsort's array is declared in AND out (`*arg:0 -> *arg:0`), so the elements' taint is never dropped at the call -- the array stays tainted, it escapes as an out-param when it is the caller's own parameter, and a base pointer the engine cannot key emits a coarse_memory_store leaf instead of vanishing silently. NOT MODELLED (deliberate, disclosed): the comparator's own dataflow (elements -> cmp's arg0/arg1 -> cmp's return value -> the resulting permutation) runs inside libc, which the engine does not analyze, so a comparator that copies a tainted element into a caller buffer, or returns an element-derived value, is not followed; the permutation is an ordering effect on the array with no separate dataflow key; and the comparator pointer argument is never treated as a sink nor descended. Modelling qsort also stops the array from being reported as an unanalyzed external frontier (and, under --unknown-call stop, from being dropped as one).

attacker-controlled length (arg3) to memccpy(dest, src, c, n)
unbounded copy of tainted source into strcpy dest
unbounded append of tainted source into strcat dest

models._comment_extra_copy: BSD/glibc copy primitives beyond the classic libc set (previously enumerated by the retired sink-sweep.sh, now modeled so `bn taint models` and the engine cover them). bcopy has REVERSED args vs memcpy -- bcopy(src, dst, n) -- so it propagates *arg:0 -> *arg:1 and its length is arg 2. mempcpy mirrors memcpy. strlcpy/strlcat are size-bounded like strncpy/strncat: a tainted size arg is the overflow sink.

sink.detail: attacker-controlled length to bcopy (src, dst, n)

models._comment_snprintf_size: snprintf/vsnprintf write AT MOST `size` bytes into the destination, so the write size (arg1) is a length sink into arg0 in its own right -- declared with the bounded-write `len_arg`/`buf_arg` pair (#443) used by the recv/read family, NOT as an extra `tainted_args` entry, which stays 'the tainted FORMAT'. `tainted_args` and the length arm share one entry and therefore one class: a tainted size is reported under `format_or_overflow`, whose own detail already covered 'size/format'. #808: without the pair the size arm was never armed while the detail claimed size coverage, so `snprintf(dst, n, "%s", "xy")` with a tainted n -- a variable-limit write into a fixed buffer -- returned reached_sinks=[] and a false all-clear, where the equivalent `strncpy(dst, "xy", n)` reported overflow_len. The declared `buf_arg` additionally lets the engine's provably-bounded relabel apply (dst=malloc(n); snprintf(dst,n,...)) instead of over-claiming.
models._comment_format_v: Plain (non-_chk) v-printf family + asprintf/dprintf (#317): the unfortified libc formatters that an internal vformatter wrapper bottoms out at -- previously only the _chk/_s variants were modeled, so a tainted format routed through e.g. a `gs_snprintf` wrapper calling plain vsnprintf passed through unflagged. v* take a va_list (no discoverable varargs); the format-string arg is the sink.
models._comment_format_chk: Fortified printf-family: leading flag/strlen (and maxlen for snprintf) args shift the format string + varargs right. v* take a va_list (no discoverable varargs), so no 'varargs'. #808: only the snprintf pair carries an attacker-settable write LENGTH -- __snprintf_chk's maxlen stays at arg1 (only the format shifts, to arg4), so it is declared as the `len_arg`/`buf_arg` pair with buf_arg=0. It is armed like the rest of the __*_chk family (#443): the fortify check aborts at runtime instead of overflowing, so the class stays this family's lower-severity `fortified_format` rather than a plain overflow. __sprintf_chk/__vsprintf_chk have NO length arg (their only size is the compiler-supplied destlen), so they keep arming just the format.
models._comment_asprintf_chk: FORTIFY asprintf/vasprintf (#373): __asprintf_chk(strp, flags, fmt, ...) and __vasprintf_chk(strp, flags, fmt, va_list). The leading `flags` arg shifts the format string to arg2 (vs arg1 in the plain asprintf/vasprintf above). asprintf has real varargs from arg3; vasprintf takes a va_list (no discoverable varargs).
models._comment_log_format: Logging formatters take a printf-style format string; a tainted format is a format-string vuln (CWE-134) that daemons/firmware hit constantly. syslog(prio, fmt, ...)/vsyslog(prio, fmt, ap): fmt=arg1. BSD err.h: err/errx(eval, fmt, ...) fmt=arg1 (verr/verrx same); warn/warnx(fmt, ...) fmt=arg0 (vwarn/vwarnx same). GLib: g_log(domain, level, fmt, ...) fmt=arg2; g_warning/g_message/g_critical/g_error/g_debug/g_info(fmt, ...) fmt=arg0.

sink.detail: tainted path to dlopen() (arbitrary library load)

models._comment_cxx_new: C++ operator new / new[] (Itanium ABI). Keyed underscore-stripped (Znwm/Znam) so the mangled symbols resolve via lookup_model, which also canonicalizes the size_t-overload (Znwm/Znwj), nothrow/aligned suffixes, and the demangled 'operator new'/'operator new[]' spellings to these two keys (#204). Like malloc, the size is arg 0. Placement new (_ZnwmPv / 'operator new(size, void*)') does not allocate and is excluded by lookup_model, so it never reaches here.

sink.detail: attacker-controlled allocation size to operator new
attacker-controlled allocation size to operator new[]

models._comment_fortified: FORTIFY_SOURCE (-D_FORTIFY_SOURCE) _chk variants. Keyed underscore-stripped so __memcpy_chk etc. resolve here (lookup_model strips leading underscores). The extra trailing destlen/objsize args are compile-time guards, not data flow. Copy/concat use the 'fortified_overflow' class: the call still aborts at runtime, so it is lower-severity than the raw variant but a tainted length/source reaching it is worth surfacing. Format _chk variants live in the format section (they also carry 'varargs').

models._comment_annex_k: C11 Annex-K / 'secure CRT' *_s variants. A destsz/bufsz guard arg follows the destination, shifting src/count/format one position right vs the classic libc functions: the copy family is (dest, destsz, src[, count]); the printf family is (buffer, bufsz, format, ...). They are bounds-checked and abort at runtime, so they reuse the lower-severity fortified_* classes of the __*_chk family. Positions follow the Annex-K signatures (NOT the Microsoft _snprintf_s(...,count,...) form) and were verified against real 32-bit ARM callsites.

models._comment_optional_sinks: Opt-in sinks: a sink with 'optional': true fires only when its 'class' is passed via --sink-class (engine: enabled_sink_classes). Off by default so 'tainted data written out' does not spam normal runs; useful when auditing persistence / file corruption / exfiltration. They are still non-empty models, so they suppress the conservative 'unmodeled external' fallback exactly like the benign {} entries they replace.

models._comment_glib: GLib (glib-2.0) allocator / dup / list helpers, common on parser paths. Without models these surface as unmodeled_callee frontier leaves and flood output (#160). Allocators mirror malloc/calloc/realloc (alloc_size sink on the byte-count arg); g_free/g_slice_free are benign. The g_str*/g_memdup helpers return a freshly-allocated copy (propagate source -> *ret); g_strlcpy/g_strlcat are size-bounded copies (propagate, no overflow sink). List helpers store the data pointer into the container (propagate the data arg -> ret).
models._comment_benign: Empty models mark functions that neither source, propagate, nor sink taint, so a tainted argument does not trigger the conservative 'unmodeled external' fallback. They cut noise without hiding real flows.
models._comment_byteorder: Byte-order and address conversions TRANSFORM their input into their return value, so taint MUST flow arg->ret. Modeling them benign ({}) let an attacker-controlled length laundered through `n = ntohl(hdr->len)` drop to untainted before reaching `memcpy(dst, src, n)`, producing a false all-clear on the most common network-parse overflow. htons/htonl/ntohs/ntohl take a scalar; inet_addr derives its result from the string it is passed.
